title: The Starry Night
subtitle: Vincent van Gogh · 1889
description: Painted from the window of his asylum room at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, van Gogh's swirling night sky is one of the most recognised paintings in Western art. The village below sleeps while the heavens churn with an almost violent energy — hope and anguish in a single canvas.

title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
subtitle: Johannes Vermeer · 1665
description: Often called the Mona Lisa of the North, Vermeer's mysterious figure glances back over her shoulder with an expression that has puzzled viewers for centuries. The luminous pearl, the soft turban, the parted lips — everything here sits on the edge of a sentence never finished.

title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
subtitle: Katsushika Hokusai · 1831
description: A towering wave of foam-tipped fingers reaches toward three fishing boats while Mount Fuji sits, tiny and serene, in the background. Hokusai distilled all of nature's indifferent power into a single frozen moment of Prussian blue and white.

title: Water Lilies (Nymphéas)
subtitle: Claude Monet · 1906
description: Monet spent the last 26 years of his life obsessively painting the pond at Giverny. This panel dissolves the boundary between water, light, and reflection until the surface becomes pure sensation — a painting you feel before you understand it.

title: The Persistence of Memory
subtitle: Salvador Dalí · 1931
description: Melting watches draped over a barren landscape make time itself feel unreliable. Dalí allegedly painted this small masterpiece after staring at a melting Camembert cheese — proof that the most disorienting ideas can come from the most ordinary moments.

title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte
subtitle: Georges Seurat · 1886
description: Built entirely from millions of tiny dots of pure colour — a technique Seurat called Pointillism — this monumental scene of Parisians at leisure rewards close inspection and wide-eyed wonder equally. Step back and the dots dissolve into shimmering afternoon light.

title: The Birth of Venus
subtitle: Sandro Botticelli · 1485
description: Venus rises from the sea on a shell, her golden hair caught by the breath of Zephyr. Painted for the Medici family, Botticelli's goddess of love remains one of the most graceful images in all of Western painting — myth made flesh in tempera and gold.

title: Impression, Sunrise
subtitle: Claude Monet · 1872
description: The painting that accidentally named an entire movement. A critic mocked its sketchiness, calling it a mere 'impression' — and the Impressionists kept the name. That small orange sun burning through the fog of Le Havre harbour is one of the most consequential brushstrokes in art history.
